description:
Research Summary

This Sheffield ECOSOLUTIONS project examines how irrigation wastewater and pesticides jointly influence antimicrobial resistance in agricultural soils and groundwater.

The advertised programme provides 45 months of doctoral funding, subject to its selection and eligibility rules.

Official Project Title

Understanding interactions between wastewater and pesticides on the fate of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in fields

Research Focus and Methods

Compare irrigation sources and use tomato soil mesocosms to study contaminants, microbial diversity and resistance. Test pesticide effects and possible mitigations, including pesticide-degrading bacteria.

Research Training and Development

Includes a three-month secondment with Defra/Fera.

Funding and Duration

How to Apply

  1. Read the official ECOSOLUTIONS programme page and the linked project advert.
  2. Use the Apply now link on the official programme page and identify the relevant project.
  3. Follow the application form’s current supporting-document instructions; the programme page does not provide a complete document checklist.
  4. Contact the project supervisor for project-specific questions.

Applications are assessed by the programme committee; shortlisted candidates are invited to online interviews. The interview date is not yet specified.
